commit_text:
Place VendorAlias first in meta_path

When other libraries or tools add items to the meta_path, we need to preempt
some of their import hooks to be sure modules can be properly found. This also
prevents problems importing built-in modules on Python 2 where it will first
attempt to import something like:

    requests.packages.chardet.sys

By placing our VendorAlias first, the above will fail and then it will fall
back to trying to import sys directly instead.
Files: requests/packages/__init__.py
Symbols: 
--- requests/packages/__init__.py
+++ requests/packages/__init__.py
@@ -107 +107 @@ class VendorAlias(object):
-sys.meta_path.append(VendorAlias(["urllib3", "chardet"]))
+sys.meta_path.insert(0, VendorAlias(["urllib3", "chardet"]))
summary: This commit fixes import failures for built-in modules on Python 2 by ensuring the VendorAlias import hook takes precedence over other third-party hooks. It modifies the requests packages module to insert the alias at the start of the system meta path, preventing incorrect module resolution attempts.

summary: This documentation update clarifies that method-level parameters, such as cookies, are not persisted across requests when using a session. It explains that users must manually manage session cookies to ensure they are sent with subsequent requests. The changes are located in the API and advanced user guides.
